steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Odysseus is the archetypal Greek hero whose intelligence (metis) is as important as his physical strength

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Odyssey tells the story of Odysseus's ten-year journey home (nostos) from the Trojan War

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Odysseus's key qualities: cunning, eloquence, endurance, bravery, curiosity and leadership

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Unlike Achilles (who chose glory and early death), Odysseus chooses survival and homecoming

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How does Odysseus differ from Achilles as a hero? | Q: Why was shouting his name to Polyphemus a fatal error? | Q: How does Penelope mirror Odysseus's character?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Achilles represents physical prowess and the pursuit of kleos (glory) through death in battle. Odysseus represents metis (cunning intelligence) and the pursuit of nostos (homecoming) through survival  | It allowed Polyphemus to call down his father Poseidon's curse on Odysseus, causing the ten-year delay. It was an act of hubris — valuing his reputation over his safety and his crew's lives. | Penelope's trick of unraveling Laertes' shroud shows the same cunning and patience as Odysseus. Like him, she uses intelligence to survive in a hostile situation.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always balance Odysseus's positive qualities with his flaws — he is a complex, not idealised, hero The Polyphemus episode is the most commonly tested — know it in detail Compare Odysseus with other characters who show (or lack) xenia, cunning or restraint Penelope and Telemachus are important secondary heroes — don't neglect them Use specific book references when possible to show detailed knowledge of the text
